# Emanuele Pane and James Shannon
Date: 2026-09-23 | Duration: 64.27999877929688m

## Summary
The team wants to overcome a current limit of 80 experiments per year, caused by technical limitations and operational fragility, while improving trust, learning, and growth. The goal is to enable squads and product managers to create and interpret experiments independently, shifting the CRO team toward strategic guidance. GrowthBook was presented as a warehouse-native platform that connects with Snowflake, supports reusable metrics, feature flags, sticky bucketing, namespaces, holdouts, 27 SDK variants, and AI-assisted Bayesian and frequentist analysis. Data integration could reuse existing Telium and Adobe Analytics pipelines through custom middleware or use GrowthBook’s managed event forwarder, with the latter involving an infrastructure fee. The three-month pilot will run during peak season, assess technical and organizational fit, improve metric and Adobe Analytics data alignment, and define resources, data flows, costs, and operating-model changes. Current benchmarks show about 25% of experiments produce an RPV lift, while the aspiration is to increase experiment volume by 50% without reducing quality.

## Keywords
experimentation, data integration, A/B testing, Growth Book, Snowflake, pilot program

## Action Items

**Emanuele Pane and Emily Simpson**
Engage in commercial discussions regarding the pilot scope and pricing details (01:02:57)

**James Shannon**
Set up Slack communication channel for ongoing collaboration with Storio Group team (01:02:17)

**James Shannon and Rémy Marin**
Lead technical pilot setup including integration of Growth Book SDK and data pipelines with Snowflake (01:01:14)

**Unassigned**
Schedule a kickoff call to define success criteria, technical requirements, and pilot timeline (01:02:40)
Arrange follow-up call(s) focused on detailed data integration scenarios and Snowflake event ingestion pipelines with Storio’s data team (01:01:10)

# Emanuele Pane and James Shannon
Date: 2026-09-30 | Duration: 36.13999938964844m

## Summary
The team is preparing a proof of concept beginning early next week with a small, skilled group from product, analytics, and engineering to assess platform fit, organizational change, experimentation strategy, and process improvements. Emanuele Pane will arrange the technical kickoff, while James Shannon will provide standard terms and data protection agreements. The POC includes enterprise features, training, support calls, and culture-building activities, with opt-out rights and no financial penalty. Its duration remains under discussion, with Emily Simpson suggesting more than 30 days and James favoring faster validation of key outcomes. The value model estimates that a 0.1% revenue-per-visitor lift could generate €340,000 per winning experiment, while increasing testing to 130 experiments could produce €4 million gross or €2 million net after decay. Pricing includes a base license and €25,000 blocks of 50 experiments, with approximately €255,000 annually for 130 experiments. Budget approval, legal review, billing alignment, technical architecture, event-forwarding costs, and software rationalization remain important next steps.

## Keywords
POC, value model, experiment licensing, legal review, fiscal year alignment, organizational complexity

Send out POC team invites for early next week technical alignment call (04:19)
Schedule the POC kickoff call with James Shannon (34:50)
